html:
Alauddin Khalji was sultan of Delhi from 1296 to 1316, the strongest ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. He took the throne by murdering his uncle and father-in-law, Sultan Jalaluddin, paid for with gold from a raid on Devagiri in the Deccan.

He faced two tasks and did both.

First, the Mongols. Armies of the Chagatai Khanate came almost every year and twice reached Delhi. He beat them at Kili in 1299 and in three more battles by 1306, and the raids stopped (see the Mongol invasions).

Second, conquest. He took Gujarat, Ranthambore, Chittor and Malwa. Then his general Malik Kafur, a former slave, marched south between 1308 and 1311 and raided as far as Madurai. He brought back hundreds of elephants and tons of gold, perhaps including the Koh-i-Noor.

To keep a huge standing army on low pay he fixed the price of grain, cloth, horses and slaves in the Delhi markets and set spies to enforce it. He took half the crop as tax, measured field by field.

He could not read. He built the Alai Darwaza beside the Qutb Minar. The tale of his siege of Chittor for Queen Padmini was written 240 years later.
